item.description: - Kinew is pressing Washington to drop tariffs now that Democrats control Congress. - Gillingham's new executive policy committee blends rookies with veterans, Browaty still chairs finance. - WestJet's new hangar near the airport means hundreds of jobs for Winnipeg. - A repeat shutdown shows Manitoba cracking down on unsafe trucking operators. - Lung cancer screening and drug call strategies are both still works in progress.

item.title: 2026-11-05 Climate Policy & Nonprofit Governance: Charity Rules Overhaul and Hydro's Drought Loss
item.description: - CRA's charity rules consultation closes December 3rd, flag it to board-sitting clients. - Watch the revocation tax changes if any client is planning a charity wind-down or merger. - Manitoba Hydro posted a $446 million loss this year, drought keeps squeezing the utility. - Hydro's $17 billion capital plan over ten years points to future rate pressure. - Budget net-zero spending and Georgia's new energy regulator are both signals for clean power money.

item.title: 2026-11-05 AI & Technology: AMD's Canadian Bet, Google's AI School Backlash
item.description: - AMD's Taalas deal shows Canadian AI chip talent getting bought, not built into standalone giants. - Google's school AI policy is drawing bipartisan political heat over bundling Search with AI tools. - US data center buildout faces real political risk after Texas's governor pledged a moratorium. - A Senate permitting bill next week could move the needle on AI infrastructure costs. - Political spending by AI firms on the midterms delivered mixed results, expect more in 2028.

item.title: 2026-11-05 Health & Fitness: Menopause Costs, Dating Violence Alert, and Muscle Repair
item.description: - Menopause symptom costs are now a documented workforce and retirement planning issue, not just a health footnote. - One in three young Canadians report dating violence, a stat worth knowing if you have teen or young adult clients. - A new muscle repair compound showed promise in mice, early days, not a human therapy yet. - Regulatory licensing delays in a high profile pediatric case are raising oversight questions in Ontario. - Worth flagging to clients: employer benefits plans increasingly need menopause and mental health coverage review.

item.title: 2026-11-05 Parenting: Manitoba Childcare Gap, CCB Rises Slightly
item.description: - Manitoba childcare shortfall now measured at 77,000 spaces, a Winnipeg coalition says. - Waitlists remain the real barrier to parents returning to work, not benefit amounts. - Canada Child Benefit rose two percent in July, smaller than last year's bump. - Under-six maximum CCB now 8,157 dollars annually, useful for cash flow projections. - Ask clients expecting a baby about childcare deposits well before leave ends.
